climbs_list.name: Côte de la Croix du Pey

story: After a day of attacks, a 15-rider break formed 95 km from the finish, including Mathieu van der Poel, Tom Pidcock, and Quinn Simmons, with only 40 riders left in the peloton. On the Suc au May, this lead group was reduced to eight. UAE Team Emirates - XRG and Netcompany INEOS controlled the peloton, limiting the gap to 1:30. Van der Poel attacked on the final climb, joined by Pidcock, Alex Baudin, and Tobias Halland Johannessen. The peloton arrived too late, allowing Van der Poel to claim his third stage win ahead of Johannessen and Pidcock.
